questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been wanting to go to New Zealand for a long time, and exchange was the perfect opportunity. I found Auckland the most interesting when looking at the courses available.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really great being there, meeting people, and getting to do stuff I could not do in Denmark, but all the admin needed to go was a bit overwhelming.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Auckland's study abroad team was really great and helped me in the capacity I needed, but it was all pretty easy to navigate so I did not need much extra help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The RAs at the university accommodation were great, and often the easiest to come to. I cannot think of any concrete help I got besides that and internationals orientation, which was around three weeks after my arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I thought it was a good orientation, especially since it was aimed specifically at internationals and told you the kind of stuff you needed to know for having a great time not just at university but in New Zealand.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several different options, where Te tirohanga o te tōangaroa and Carlaw have guaranteed space for internationals.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Some have meal plans, but that's mostly for first years. TT had shared kitchens for all the residents.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would recommend it, even though it is a bit pricy, since it is where I met my best friends of the entire stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Te tirohanga o te tōangaroa where I lived was a bit cheaper and I think you could feel that. There were shared kitchens that you had to equip yourself, while being around a lot of people that did not know how to clean up after themselves. On the other hand I met my best friend in those kitchens, so there is some good stuff and some bad.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found the application process easy, but the course catalogue was a bit confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember the exact details, but about a week before the registration opened, they held a really helpful zoom call for all the internationals to explain it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: That zoom call was available, and then the study abroad team were also really good at replying when you needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I wanted. I did have to apply for a concession for one of them, but that was easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply as soon as they open for applications, and use their schedule tool to make sure the classes you want fit in one schedule together

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied, although taking four classes could at some points be pretty disorienting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses meant for second years, but they were taught along with third years, so the level matched pretty well with being 4th semestre, though the other 2nd years were on their 3rd semestre.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the style was kind of similar, but the seminar classes were definitely bigger, which made it harder to have good discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ENGLISH 214: Early Texts: Modern Inventions
ENGLISH 248: Popular Fiction
ENGLISH 265: Shakespeare: Comedies and Tragicomedies
HISTORY 225: Samurai and Scholars: Early Modern China and Japa

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Shakespeare course was amazing, in general I would look out for any class that Dr. Barbara Taylor teaches, she was such a good teacher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not plan on doing as much hiking as I ended up doing. I would definitely recommend bringing some gear, since it truly would be a shame to go such a beautiful place and not seeing any of it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Ironically restaurants were really cheap, which is why I ended up spending so much money on food, as I cooked a lot less than I usually would, preferring to eat out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were really great, there were so many different opportunities based on what you like.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had tons of different opportunities, organised in clubs. On top of that the school has a gym, queer-, and cultural spaces for students to find like minded people

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There were a few opportunities specifically for internationals, here I got to go to a Marae and learn about Maori culture, which was definitely great. Otherwise, I would recommend joining SASS and just finding clubs that match your interests. You can find the clubs on the uni's website or at the club expo at the start of the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I definitely recommend doing some hikes, whether day hikes or longer. For day hikes I think Waiheke and Rangitoto are perfect. I also did a longer hike on Great Barrier Island which was amazing. In Auckland I recommend Auckland gallery and Gus Fisher gallery.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, going to a Marae helped, since it helped me understand how to be respectful towards the Maori people on their land.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: To be honest, I mostly hung out with internationals, but the locals I did meet were through classes, accommodation and clubs. I definitely recommend trying to talk to people as a lot of the locals already have friend groups and are not looking for friends in the same way, so being the one to reach out is definitely the way to go.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I do not think there was a lot of big challenges, especially since I am quite interested in culture and had looked up quite a lot before getting there. I think one political thing is that their environmental efforts are much more about wildlife conservation, than things like trash sorting. This is not necessarily negative but just different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the clear steps to put Maori culture at the forefront of Kiwi culture at large, even through small things like writing a lot of sign in Maori first and introductions to classes in Maori.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have enough money, be open to people and opportunities, and do some research about the place before going, so that you know what you want out of your experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I cannot think of any big things, if you are queer, I would check out queerspace, it made me feel very at home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and knowing I can make it in a whole knew place, knowing nobody.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had a family emergency at home, and dealing with that through the distance was very difficult. I would maybe recommend talking a plan through with your family for if anything was to happen, while you are gone.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it, it will be amazing!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
